comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C15-C17, C47-C49, C83-C85 regarding risk stratification and model performance. Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers explicitly endorsing the model's ability to stratify patients into low, moderate, and high-risk categories as a key strength.

Both address validation claims C18-C19, C50-C54. OpenEval finds the validation results supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, emphasizing that single-country validation is insufficient and broader multi-country validation is needed for generalizability.

Both evaluate claims C20, C66, C99-C101 about independence from intraprocedural factors. OpenEval rates as uncertain due to contradiction with established literature, while peer reviewers support this finding, viewing the pre-procedural nature as a key advantage over existing scores.

Perfect agreement on claims C26-C30 regarding PEP diagnostic criteria. Both evaluations support the use of standard Cotton criteria without concerns about outcome definitions or severity classification.

High overlap on baseline data claims C34-C35, C132-C134, C136. Both evaluations support the PEP incidence and severity distribution findings. Peer reviewers note sufficient sample size as a strength, implicitly accepting the observed rates.

Both address study design claims C7-C8, C21, C23-C25, C155. OpenEval finds the design supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, emphasizing significant limitations including single-center/single-country design and concerns about excluded cases limiting applicability.

Both evaluate statistical analysis claims C9-C14, C37-C46. OpenEval supports the methodology and results. Peer reviewers also support these findings, explicitly recognizing the model's value as a pre-procedural prediction tool and distinguishing it favorably from intraprocedural scores.

Both address clinical utility claims C68-C70, C102, C154. OpenEval supports the potential clinical applications with appropriate qualifications. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse these utility claims, noting the model can help identify when experienced endoscopists can proceed or when referral is needed.

Both evaluate data quality and missing data claims C64-C65, C78, C82. OpenEval supports the minimal missing data claims, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting that many cases were excluded and questioning whether the score can be applied to those patients.

Both address geographic limitation and need for external validation (C79-C81, C80, C104). OpenEval supports acknowledging this limitation. Peer reviewers also support this, explicitly emphasizing the need for multi-country validation on large patient numbers.

Both evaluate comparison to existing scoring systems (C139-C143, C4-C6). OpenEval supports the criticism of prior systems' complexity. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, questioning whether the literature review is adequate and suggesting the comparison may rely on outdated references.
OpenEval evaluates diagnostic criteria for CP and IPMN (C31, C113-C115) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific diagnostic criteria claims.

OpenEval evaluates sample size calculation methodology (C32-C33, C120-C121) as supported with adequate statistical power. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates the biological explanation for pancreatic calcification's negative association with PEP (C60-C63, C144) as supported and biologically plausible. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates the explanation for negative NSAID findings (C93-C98, C145-C146) as supported, noting dose and population differences. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval evaluates the classification decision for pancreatic stent placement (C91-C92, C147-C148) as methodologically sound. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates the model's flexibility in handling planned vs. unplanned pancreatic duct procedures (C150-C152) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates statistical methods for model development and validation (C126-C131) as appropriate and standard. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
OpenEval evaluates background information about PEP severity and ERCP risks (C1-C3, C72-C74) as well-established and supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates prior literature context (C4-C6, C104) as appropriate justification for the study. Peer reviewers partially address this in R11 but question the adequacy of literature review, suggesting reliance on outdated references.
OpenEval evaluates ethical procedures for retrospective study (C22, C106-C108) as appropriate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these ethical considerations.
